title: Killed job is restarted by its scheduler

brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not reach its model to produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 363653 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, idle in transaction, txn open 4.1s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 0% over 30s (120/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $18,400/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 363653) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $18,400/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: The trade-off analysis (BIZ-5) now shows expected remaining runtime ~596s, causing ~$182,743 in checkout revenue loss at the current degradation rate, which EXCEEDS the 60s business tolerance (BIZ-1). Checkout is at 0% over 30s (BIZ-4), with $18,400/min at risk. The blocking workload is replayable (BIZ-2: replayable=True, may_interrupt policy) and idempotent, so termination only costs a 2-minute replay. No protected settlements are in flight (DB-2). These new facts make 'wait' untenable since the blocker's projected duration far exceeds the 60s degradation window the business tolerates.

audit.report: A killed job was restarted by its scheduler and its worker (pid 363653, batch_replayable_price_sync) went idle in transaction, holding a lock that blocked checkout sessions. Checkout fell from 53% success (32/60 in 15s) to 0% over 30s (120/120 failed), with $18,400/min at risk against a 95% SLO and a 60s degradation tolerance. The Database Guardian first proposed waiting because the blocker had been open only 4.1s, then switched to terminating the replayable, idempotent job once the expected remaining runtime (~596s) and ~$182,743 loss exceeded the business tolerance. The Continuity Guardian could not reach its model provider and failed closed, so the matter was escalated to pricing and the termination was not executed. The business is not back: checkout remained at 0% and the escalate action was not executed after 370.9s.
audit.root_cause: batch_replayable_price_sync (pid 363653) was idle in transaction holding a lock, blocking checkout sessions and driving checkout success to 0%.
lessons: For batch_replayable_price_sync, set a hard wait ceiling equal to the 60s business tolerance; if the blocker's expected remaining runtime (~596s) exceeds it, terminate immediately instead of waiting to gather tradeoff data, since the job is replayable, idempotent, and may_interrupt.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian reasoned correctly by pivoting from wait to terminate once the 60s tolerance invariant was violated, but it spent its only round waiting before computing the tradeoff, and the Continuity Guardian's model failure forced a fail-closed escalation, so the termination was never executed.
follow_ups: Have pricing confirm whether pid 363653 (batch_replayable_price_sync) was terminated and whether checkout success has returned to the 95% SLO.
Add a fallback grounding path for the Continuity Guardian and a pre-approved termination playbook for replayable batch workloads like price_sync.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker pid 363653 has been idle in transaction for only 4.1s (DB-1). Checkout over the last 15s succeeded 32/60 (53%) with 28 timeouts (TEL-1). The business SLO is 95% and tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout (BIZ-1). Given the blocker duration is well within the tolerated window, waiting allows natural recovery while we gather tradeoff data before considering termination.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker completes naturally, the 12 waiting sessions will be released and checkout success should improve toward the SLO. If the blocker persists beyond 60s, checkout will remain degraded and revenue at risk will continue.
proposal.risk_assessment: The blocker may not finish within the 60s business tolerance window, leading to prolonged checkout degradation and continued revenue loss. Terminating the blocker without registry evidence could cause unintended side effects.
